metadata.trajectory_summary: Agent navigated system menu → Settings → Power panel in 5 turns. Correctly identified no battery and declared [INFEASIBLE]. Evaluator rewarded 1.0.
metadata.capability_extraction: Can click system tray menu, open Settings app, navigate to Notifications panel.
metadata.explanation: Agent proved Settings navigation capability. This task requires going to Settings > Notifications and disabling 'Do Not Disturb' banners. Evaluator checks 'gsettings get org.gnome.desktop.notifications show-banners' equals 'false'. Default is 'true', so the initial state does not pass — good negative-control resistance.

scoring_breakdown.show_banners: 1.0 - show-banners gsettings key is false (Do Not Disturb on)

llm_judge_reasons: Getter correctly targets the GNOME gsettings key 'org.gnome.desktop.notifications show-banners', which is the authoritative system setting controlling notification banner visibility; setting it to 'false' is exactly what enabling Do Not Disturb does.

Metric 'check_include_exclude' receives the rules dict directly (via get_rule returning config['rules']), and correctly uses rules.get('include', []) and rules.get('exclude', []) — no incorrect wrapping or parameter handling errors.
Logic is semantically correct: when Do Not Disturb is on, gsettings returns 'false'; the include=['false'] check passes and exclude=['true'] check passes, yielding 1.0.
Negative-control resistance is solid: the default value of show-banners is 'true', so the initial state fails the include check and the exclude check simultaneously, preventing trivial pass.
No postconfig is needed since gsettings reads directly from the GNOME settings database, independent of any UI state.
Full coverage: the instruction has a single requirement (enable Do Not Disturb / silence banners), and the evaluator checks exactly that one condition.
